statements.statement: The video being circulated as an attack on the French embassy in Sudan is actually an eight-year-old video from September 2012 in Khartoum, Sudan, when demonstrators stormed the German embassy, as confirmed by a CNN video report from September 14, 2012, and a news report from the German newspaper Der Tagesspiegel dated September 14, 2012, which shows demonstrators storming and setting fire to the German embassy.
statements.support_span: An eight-year-old video showing protestors attack the German embassy in Sudan is being peddled as a recent attack on the French embassy in the country. | On breaking the video into key-frames and performing a reverse image search using Google, we found news reports which show that the visual footage is from Sudan in September 2012 when demonstrators stormed the German embassy in the capital Khartoum | We found a news report [https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/proteste-gegen-anti-islam-film-demonstranten-setzen-deutsche-botschaft-im-sudan-in-brand/7132474.html] by German Newspaper Der Tagesspiegel dated September 14th, 2012 which had the same visuals as in the viral clip which stated that in Sudan, demonstrators stormed the German embassy and set it on fire | We also found a video report by CNN on the incident which had the same visuals as the viral clip and reported on September 14, 2012, that protestors were able to overpower security forces to breach the walls of the German embassy in Khartoum, Sudan.

statements.statement: The 2012 protests in Sudan were triggered by a US film titled 'Innocence of Muslims' which was critical of Islam, and during the incident, protesters breached the German embassy gates, attacked the facade, tore down the flag, and replaced it with a black Islamic flag before setting fire to the building.
statements.support_span: It also states that the privately made American film, called "Innocence of Muslims," portrays the prophet Muhammad as a womanizer, homosexual and child abuser due to which the protests had broken out. | The report further stated that protesters threw stones at the two neighboring outposts in Khartoum before they stormed the main gates of the German embassy and attacked its facade and tore down the flag, replacing it with a black Islamic one before setting fire to the building.

silver.justification: The evidence indicates that the video being circulated as an attack on the French embassy in Sudan is actually footage from September 2012. Multiple sources, including a news report from Der Tagesspiegel and a CNN video report, confirm that the visuals depict demonstrators storming and setting fire to the German embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, following protests triggered by the film 'Innocence of Muslims.' Therefore, the claim misidentifies both the target embassy and the timing of the event shown in the video.
